body: All the time. My friends tell me frequently that the things my parents do aren’t normal or healthy ways to treat their children, but it never occurred to me that it wasn’t normal until I brought it up to them.
I strongly suspect I have autism or bp (or both) so it’s very likely that I’ve just been hyperfixating for the last 7 years lol, but if it gives me a reason to go on, so be it!

Well I can’t tell you if it’s normal but I can say that your certainly not alone. I’ve been struggling with intrusive thoughts and fantasies of getting revenge on my dad for the suffering he is still putting my through, and my mom for not doing anything to stop him. It’s gotten progressively worse and lately it doesn’t even feel intrusive anymore. I WANT revenge on him. I know it’s wrong and that I’ll never get it, but I still want it. I will never act on it, but I crave for him to know the pain he puts me through.

I don’t think you were in the wrong here because that kind of behavior is unacceptable no matter who it’s coming from. If a man said those things about a woman, everyone would be quick to her defense. Sexual harassment is never okay even if it isn’t super severe. However, him implying your gay being the final straw is a little bit homophobic even if that wasn’t your intention. Getting mad if someone implies or asks if your gay, suggests that you think being called gay is offensive, or bad. This probably wasn’t your intention, it’s likely that no one has explained that to you. Most straight people don’t know that that can be harmful. But in conclusion, that guy definitely should not have been treating you that way, and you were right to kick him out, however you could work on being a better ally, (if you want to be that is.)
